name: Moodlet System
description: Aggregates recent events into stacking, timed mood modifiers — 'promoted: +2 happy for 4 hours', 'grudge formed: -3 for a day' — and resolves the stack into a single mood value everything else reads. Moodlets are additive and individually expiring rather than a mood number pushed around directly, because a sim who was promoted and then stepped in a puddle should feel both, and 'mood = 5' cannot hold two truths at once. Sources apply moodlets by emitting their own events; this component maps event payloads to configured moodlet definitions, so adding a new cause is a table entry, not a code path. It owns the stack and the resolved mood only: it does not change what the sim does — autonomy (utility.behavior_fsm) and needs (social.needs_decay) listen for moodlet application and adjust their own behavior, keeping the arrow of causation one-directional and cycle-free.

inputs.name: moodletDefinitions
inputs.description: Moodlet types: id, mood delta, duration, and stack rule (refresh, stack, ignore-duplicate). The stack rule is per-definition because 'well-rested' should refresh while 'embarrassed' should pile up.

inputs.name: maxActiveMoodlets
inputs.description: Cap on simultaneously active moodlets; the weakest drops off when full. Prevents degenerate stacking and bounds the mood panel's height.

inputs.name: moodBands
inputs.description: Thresholds mapping the summed stack to named mood bands. Consumers read the band, not the sum, so display and gameplay never disagree about what counts as happy.

outputs.name: activeMoodlets
outputs.description: The live stack with remaining durations, for the mood panel and for save-state round-tripping.

outputs.name: currentMood
outputs.description: The resolved mood band id — the single value career performance, autonomy, and dialogue tone all key off.
